description:
Deterministically review the source of a screen before presenting it. For every dashboard, call this after get-review-rules and before check-comprehension. In a project with an installed components folder, call it for every screen you build, before you show the first screenshot, with `type: "screen"` when the screen is no dashboard. A prose self-review is not a substitute.

Pass the complete page source. The rules follow what the page is built on. Pass `installedComponents`, the list of files in the project's components/ui folder, for any screen: the tool then names each control the page builds by hand though the design system ships it, such as a menu, tabs, a segmented control, a badge, an avatar, a search input, a table, a card, a kanban board, a dialog or a toast. Each one is a serious finding. Swap it for the installed part, or pass the control and the reason in `keptHandBuilt` when the installed part cannot work. A page built on an installed Better Design kit is also held to the kit's dashboard components: pass the installed Sidebar, StatCard, and Table source files too. A one-file HTML page or another framework is not, and those rules come back as not applicable. Pass `fixture` and `interpretation` only when the request itself supplied them; never write one from the page. Without them the page keeps its own title, actions and structure, and the reply lists what a dense page must still show, with a measurement when the source shows many figures at one size and none larger. The tool fails incomplete source, rewritten fixture copy, unsupported claims, missing or under-composed installed components, hand-built controls beside an installed design system, raw aside/table markup in a kit page, the wrong scan order, action color on every rate, and stepper rails on short flows.

FAIL is blocking and returns an MCP tool error. Fix every finding and call the tool again until PASS. NOT APPLICABLE is not a failure: keep the page as it is and finish with check-comprehension and inspect-spacing. For a kit dashboard built from a request fixture, call finalize-dashboard-review after PASS; only its VALID source-bound receipt permits presentation.

componentSources.description: Installed Sidebar, StatCard, and Table source files for compound-composition review.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

fixture.description: Only when the request supplied one: its unchanged fixture object. The first step is the overview; remaining steps are dependent task screens. Omit it when fixing an existing page.

installedComponents.description: The path of every file in the project's installed components folder, such as src/components/ui/tabs.tsx. Paths only, no content. With it the tool checks any screen for controls built by hand.

interpretation.description: Only when the request asked for one: the supplied or factually derived takeaway that must appear after records.

keptHandBuilt.description: Only after a hand-built finding you cannot fix: each control you keep by hand, and why. The report repeats the reason.

control.description: The control as the finding names it: kanban board, search input, segmented control, menu, tabs, dialog, toast, table, badge, avatar, card.

reason.description: Why the installed part cannot work here, in one sentence.

screen.description: What this screen is, e.g. 'funnel report overview'.

source.description: Complete source for the page: TSX, JSX, or the whole HTML file.

type.description: 'screen' for a page that is no dashboard or overview: only the hand-built control check runs, so pass installedComponents. Defaults to 'dashboard'.
